53-017.r: Bipin Chandra Pal → Extremist; Pherozeshah Mehta and Gokhale → Moderates. Tilak too was not a Moderate. Extremist leaders: Lajpat Rai, Tilak, Pal, Aurobindo Ghose.
53-017.h: Lal-Bal-Pal + Aurobindo = the four Extremist pillars.

53-019.r: Lala Lajpat Rai → 'Sher-e-Punjab', also 'Punjab Kesari'; Extremist of Punjab (Lal-Bal-Pal), not a Moderate.

53-021.r: Lala Lajpat Rai → took Italian revolutionary Mazzini as his political guru; translated Mazzini's 'The Duty of Man' into Urdu.

53-022.r: Lala Lajpat Rai → wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi, Shivaji, Shrikrishna and Dayanand; lived in America in exile; elected to Central Assembly; wrote 'Unhappy India'.

53-023.r: Lala Lajpat Rai → called Congress sessions the "Annual National Festival of Educated Indians".

53-024.r: Bal Gangadhar Tilak → an Extremist (pioneer of the Lal-Bal-Pal neo-nationalists), not a Moderate; Gokhale, A.O. Hume and Malviya were not Extremists.

53-025.r: Aurobindo Ghosh → main leader of the Swadeshi Movement (1905, against Bengal partition), with Lajpat Rai, Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.

53-026.r: Lokmanya Tilak → called 'Father of Indian Unrest' by Valentine Chirol; Tilak's defamation suit against Chirol in England failed.

53-030.r: Max Muller → pleaded for mercy for the sentenced Tilak: "As a great scholar of Sanskrit, I am interested in Tilak."

53-031.r: Tilak became 'Lokmanya' through several events, e.g. accused in the Rand–Ayerst murder case, 18 months' rigorous imprisonment, came out a national hero → 'More than one'.

53-032.r: Bal Gangadhar Tilak → sentenced in 1908 to 6 years' imprisonment; deported to Mandalay Jail, Burma.

53-034.r: Extremist ideology → self-government by aggressive means instead of petitions and constitutional ways; independence meant complete freedom from foreign control.

53-035.r: Indian Muslims stayed away from the extremist movement → extremists harped on the Hindu part (Aurobindo: only Hindu religion will fulfil the aim of independence).

53-036.r: A false, R true: Tilak was a nationalist, not a communalist; he used religion as a political weapon, starting Ganapati and Shivaji festivals in Maharashtra.

53-040.r: Tilak's bier (died 1 August 1920) → lifted by Gandhi with Shaukat Ali and Dr. Saifuddin Kichlew; Maulana Hasrat Mohani read the elegy.

54-001.r: 'Abhinav Bharat' secret revolutionary society → V.D. Savarkar; his 'Mitra Mela' merged into it at Nasik (Maharashtra) in 1904. He wrote 'The Indian War of Independence 1857'.

54-008.r: V.D. Savarkar → set up a branch of Abhinav Bharat Society at India House, London, in 1906.

54-009.r: All true of V.D. Savarkar: founded Abhinav Bharat; wrote Mazzini's biography; wrote 'The Indian War of Independence 1857' (First War of Independence); jumped from a ship to escape.

54-010.r: Rashtriya Swayamsewak Sangh → founded by Keshav Baliram Hedgewar on 27 September 1925 at Nagpur (its headquarters).

54-011.r: Yugantar Party → led by Jatindranath Mukherjee ('Bagha Jatin', 1879-1915).

54-012.r: Anushilan Samiti → Calcutta branch (1902) by Pramath Nath (P.) Mitra with Bagha Jatin and Barindra Ghosh; first at Midnapur (Gyanendra Nath Basu); Dhaka branch 1906 (Pulin Bihari Das).

54-013.r: Sachindra Nath Sanyal → set up a branch of Anushilan Samiti at Patna in 1913.

54-015.r: Barindra Ghosh (Aurobindo's younger brother) → his activities gave birth to the revolutionary Anushilan Samiti; Aurobindo wrote the pamphlet 'Bhawani Mandir' (1905).

54-019.r: Tilak became 'Lokmanya' in the revolutionary phase: arrested July 1897 for sedition (Sec 124-A) after Rand–Ayerst murders by Chapekar brothers; 18 months' jail caused nationwide protests.

54-020.r: Barrah Dacoity (1908, Dhaka district) → first major venture of revolutionary terrorists in East Bengal; planned by Pulin Behari Das.

54-021.r: Attempt on Kingsford (Chief Presidency Magistrate) → Muzaffarpur, Bihar, 30 April 1908, by Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki, bombing a carriage outside the European club.

54-024.r: Alipore Conspiracy Case (1908; 49 accused, 19 sentenced) → Aurobindo Ghosh brilliantly defended and freed by Chittaranjan Das.

54-025.r: Hindustan Republican Association → founded at Kanpur, October 1924; Sachindranath Sanyal (President), Ramprasad Bismil, Jogesh Chatterjee, Chandra Shekhar Azad.

54-027.r: Shiv Verma → not in HRA; joined its renewed form HSRA; got life imprisonment in Lahore Conspiracy. Bhagat Singh, Azad, Bismil were HRA members.

54-028.r: Ramprasad Bismil (Kakori case) → refused milk on the eve of his execution: "Now, I shall take my mother's milk only."
54-028.c: UPPSC first accepted option (c) but later removed this question.

54-029.r: "Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil me hai" → written by Bismil Azimabadi (Saiyad Shah Muhammad Hasan, born 1901, Patna); published in 'Sabah' magazine, 1922.
54-029.t: 'Bismil' here = Bismil Azimabadi, not Ram Prasad Bismil.

54-031.r: Kakori Conspiracy (HRA looted government treasury at Kakori, 9 August 1925) → Ram Prasad Bismil hanged; Chandra Shekhar Azad alone escaped arrest.

54-036.r: Surya Sen → not linked with Kakori incident; Ram Prasad Bismil, Rajendra Lahiri and Ashfaq Ullah were.

54-037.r: Bhagat Singh → not part of Kakori Conspiracy; Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh and Asfaqullah Khan were.

54-038.r: Kakori Conspiracy Case (train robbery near Lucknow, 9 August 1925) → Government advocate (public prosecutor) Jagat Narain Mulla.

54-039.r: Kanpur Conspiracy Case 1924 (against communists) → accused incl. M.N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shaukat Usmani, S.A. Dange, Nalini Gupta; not M.A. Ansari.

54-040.r: "Daro-deewar pe hasrat ki nazar karte hain, khush raho ahle-vatan ham to safar karte hain" → Wazid Ali Shah, last Nawab of Awadh; revolutionaries sang it in prison.
54-040.t: Not Bismil or Ashfaqullah; they only sang it.

54-041.r: Hindustan Socialist Republican Association → formed September 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi, under Chandra Shekhar Azad; Bhagat Singh with Batukeshwar Dutt bombed the Central Assembly.

54-046.r: HSRA founders → Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Shiv Verma, Jai Dev Kapoor, Vijay Kumar Singh under Azad; HRA renamed HSRA, September 1928, Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.

54-049.r: No 'Hindustan Socialist Democratic Union' existed; the 1928 body of Bhagat Singh, Azad, Sachindra Sanyal was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
54-049.c: No answer printed: wrong organisation name and no correct option; UPPSC's initial key said (b).

54-050.r: Chandrasekhar Azad → killed by police bullets in an encounter at Alfred Park, 27 February 1931; the only HSRA member never arrested.

54-051.r: 'Inquilab Zindabad' (Long Live Revolution) → written by Maulavi Hasrat Mohani; first used and popularised by Bhagat Singh.
54-051.t: Coined by Hasrat Mohani, made popular by Bhagat Singh.

54-054.r: Bhagat Singh (born September 1907) → a little over 21 when he and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly, 8 April 1929.

54-055.r: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev → executed on 23 March 1931. Assembly bomb (8 April 1929, with Batukeshwar Dutt) was low-intensity, caused no deaths; they surrendered.

54-056.r: Bhagat Singh's memorial → Hussainiwala, Ferozpur district, on the Sutlej, where he, Rajguru and Sukhdev were cremated after hanging on 23 March 1931.

54-057.r: Lahore Conspiracy → Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev sentenced to death (October 1930), hanged 23 March 1931; Batukeshwar Dutt not hanged, sent to Cellular Jail (Kala Pani).

54-061.r: Ashfaq Ullah Khan (born Shahjahanpur) → first recorded Muslim hanged for India's freedom: 19 December 1927, Faizabad Jail, aged 27.
54-061.t: If 1857 is counted, Mughal prince Azizuddin was hanged first.

54-062.r: Order: Lahore case (first, 1916) → Kanpur case (1924) → Kakori case (1925) → Meerut case (1929). Second Lahore case: 1930.

54-063.r: Wrong pair: Kakori Conspiracy was 9 August 1925, not 1924. Correct: Howrah Conspiracy 1910; Victoria Conspiracy 1914; Lahore Conspiracy 1916 and 1930.

54-064.r: Wrong pair: Nasik Conspiracy → Anant Lakshman Kanhare (Abhinav Bharat), not Ras Bihari Bose (Delhi Conspiracy). Correct: Delhi–Amirchand; Kakori–Ashfaqulla; Lahore–Jatin Das.

54-065.r: Howrah Conspiracy → Jatindranath Mukherjee; Lahore Conspiracy → Rajguru; Delhi Conspiracy → Master Ami Chand; Alipore Conspiracy → Aurobindo Ghosh.

54-066.r: Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case → S.A. Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Shaukat Usmani and Nalini Gupta jailed, four years each.

54-067.r: Chittagong Armoury Raid → organised by Surya Sen ('Master Da') through his Indian Republican Army, 18 April 1930.

54-071.r: Youngest martyr among options → Khudiram Bose, hanged 11 August 1908 aged 18 years 8 months (Hemu Kalani 19, Sukhdev 23, Ashfaqullah 27).

54-072.r: Abhinav Bharat Society → V.D. Savarkar; Anushilan Samiti → Sri Aurobindo Ghosh; Gadar Party → Lala Hardayal; Swaraj Party → C.R. Das.

54-073.r: Book's key: Abhinav Bharat → G.D. Savarkar; Mitra Mela → V.D. Savarkar; Indian Republican Army → S. Sen (Surya Sen); Hindustan Republican Association → S.N. Sanyal.
54-073.c: Both bodies were founded by the Savarkar brothers (Mitra Mela later became Abhinav Bharat), and V.D. Savarkar is usually named for both. Code (d) is the only one fitting Surya Sen and Sanyal.

54-074.r: Chittagong Armoury Raid → Surya Sen (18 April 1930); Kakori → Ram Prasad Bismil (9 August 1925); Lahore Conspiracy → Jatin Das (1929); Ghadar Party → Lala Hardayal (1913).

54-075.r: Jatin Das → arrested 14 June 1929 in the supplementary Lahore Conspiracy Case; died after a 63-day hunger strike for jail reforms.

54-077.r: End of life: Jatin Das → hunger strike; Chandrashekhar Azad → encounter; Bhagat Singh → hanged; Kalpana Dutt → during life imprisonment (book's key).

54-078.r: Chittagong Armoury Raid → Kalpana Dutt (arrested with Surya Sen, life imprisonment); Abhinav Bharat → V.D. Savarkar; Anushilan Samiti → Aurobindo Ghosh; Kuka Movement → Guru Ram Singh.

54-079.r: Kakori Case Defence Committee → headed by Govind Ballabh Pant (per Yogesh Chandra Chatterjee's 'In Search of Freedom'); UPPSC's revised key.
54-079.t: A PIB article names Motilal Nehru as president; UPPSC first chose him, then revised to Pant.

54-080.r: Revolt Group → Surya Sen; Hindustan Republican Association → Ram Prasad Bismil; Hindustan Socialist Republican Association → Chandra Shekhar Azad; Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha → Bhagat Singh.

54-081.r: Naujawan Bharat Sabha → founded March 1926 by Bhagat Singh with Chhabil Das, Yaspal, Bhagwati Charan Vohra; Ambika Chakravarti (Chittagong group) was not an early member.
